Which model is worth the money

Every language model we can measure, plotted by how capable it is against what it costs to run. One chart per kind of work.

  • ↑Higher is more capable
  • ←Further left is cheaper
  • The dashed line is the best deal at each level — nothing beats a model on it for price and power at once

Showing every model released so far, up to 2026-11-22 — today’s ranking.

What the date slider and play button do

Press play to watch the field arrive: the run starts at the oldest week, steps a week at a time and stops at today. 1× cycles through half, normal and double speed, and grabbing the slider — or pressing an arrow key on it — takes over and stops the run. If your system asks for reduced motion the run steps more slowly and the points stop popping.

The axes never move and each point keeps the ability today’s boards give it, so what changes along the run is who is on the market — not what any one of them scores.

Drag it to ask the same question as of an older date: every chart, frontier, ranking table and preset cut then shows only the models that had been released by then, with the frontier, the capability-per-cost ladder and the cuts re-solved over that pool — so the answer is the one this page would have given at that date, not today’s numbers with rows deleted. There are no historical board snapshots here: every date is scored with today’s captures, which is a reading of what an older shortlist looks like under what we know now, not a reconstruction of what the boards said then. Models released in the 30 days before the selected date carry the green ring the chart legend calls new at this date. The evidence folds at the foot of the page — prices, cost ratios, the free pool and the per-model drilldown — always list the full catalogue.

One step is one week. Each stop is a Sunday, the last day of an ISO week, and an arrow key moves one week; the ticks under the slider are the weeks and the names on them are the months. There are 20 stops, 12 Jul 2026 to now (2026-11-22).

The axes never move. Both are fixed to the range today’s field needs, and every point is drawn at the capability today’s evidence gives it, at every date — so an early date is a sparse corner of the same picture, with the space up and to the right still empty, and what the eye follows is the field filling it rather than the gridlines sliding about. A re-fit over an older pool would rescale each board on that pool’s own median and spread, which floats a model upward for no reason but the absence of the models above it; what stays per-date is what the pool genuinely decides — which points are on the frontier, where each sits on the capability-per-cost ladder, which are too thinly measured, and the preset cuts read off that ladder. Points arriving pop in with a green ring; points not yet released shrink away.

Why it stops at 12 Jul 2026. 5 Jul 2026 is not offered: its thinnest task group has 7 scored variants and 6 of them able to anchor a frontier, under the 8 and 1 this page will draw a ranking from. A week is offered only where every task group has at least 8 scored variants and at least 1 of them carrying enough of that group’s benchmark weight to anchor its frontier, and the walk stops at the first week that fails, so the offered range is one unbroken run. Coding-experiments is what binds: its boards are run on models the harnesses added late, so an older pool is plotted there but almost none of it can hold a line.

What this page is, and where the numbers come from

It is the working answer to one question: which model each step of the AI Inventor pipeline should be dialled at, and at what reasoning effort. Every model is plotted as raw capability — a 0-100 ability fitted over the public leaderboards that variant was itself measured on — against effective cost, the geometric mean of its relative list price and its relative cost per finished task, with the reference model at 1x. A model that offers several reasoning efforts is counted once per effort, because the price and the capability both move with it.

The dashed line is the Pareto frontier over those two numbers: nothing plotted beats a point on it for both cost and capability at once. Boards captured 2026-06-04 to 2026-11-22; prices are list prices from the model catalogue. Everything behind these numbers — how each board is scaled, how thin evidence is handled, and why the only thing that keeps a model off a chart is a board nobody ran it on — is in How this is judged and the evidence folds at the foot of the page.

How to read this chart

What this group is. Every live board both captures carry, read at once. The preference half is the seventeen Arena boards still published with this month's models — the whole text arena, its category slices, the text factuality vote, the WebDev arena and the Agent arena's six measures — and the capability half is every Artificial Analysis board the v2 Free route serves us that does not repeat one already in (the §4 duplicate check, r above 0.98): Intelligence Index v5 and the Strategy & Ops, Legal and Healthcare & Medical Capability Indexes (pairwise r 0.91 to 0.978), each board sharing its half equally. Engineering repeats the Intelligence Index (r 0.994), Finance and Economics repeat Legal (0.990, 0.990), so those three stay out. Nothing is chosen for a kind of work, so this is the tab to read for a model you would ask anything.

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

64 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used — which boards bought this score

Weights are the flattened ones the ranker multiplies by, so the column sums to 1.000. Models covered counts the paid variants carrying a score on that board, out of every paid variant ranked. Style control is Arena's adjustment for length and formatting habit, and it is a property of the capture, not of the board.

Across those flattened weights the pillars carry capability 50%, preference 50% — equal halves by construction, with each pillar's boards sharing its half equally unless the group says otherwise.

boardpillarweightwhat it measuressourcecapturedstyle controlmodels coveredwhat would make it wrong
AA Healthcare & Medical Indexcapability0.125Clinical knowledge and record synthesis: AA-Omniscience medical knowledge 25%, AA-Briefcase 25%, MLCR long-context reasoning 15%, AutomationBench 15%, non-hallucination 10%, HLE-Diamond 10%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: healthcare_and_medical_index (99 models)2026-11-22not applicable99 of 309The only index carrying MLCR, AA's long-context reasoning run, and run on fewer models than the others (it needs every component).
AA Intelligence Index v5capability0.125Artificial Analysis' composite of its re-run reasoning, knowledge and coding evaluations, per reasoning effort: version 5.0, which replaced v4.3 by 28 Oct 2026 and is scored only on the models AA has re-run on it.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: intelligence_index_v5 (112 models)2026-11-22not applicable112 of 309A composite, so it moves when its components saturate. Terminal- Bench 4.0 is one of its nine components, so a group weighting both reads that run twice; the Engineering Index tracks it at r 0.994, which is why no group weights the two together.
AA Legal Indexcapability0.125Legal recall and long-document work: AA-Omniscience legal knowledge 30%, AA-Briefcase 25%, HLE-Diamond 15%, non-hallucination 15%, GDP.pdf long-context documents 10%, AutomationBench 5%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: legal_index (119 models)2026-11-22not applicable119 of 309The least agentic index (30% tool loops) and the heaviest on factuality and long documents, but the knowledge it recalls is law, not this pipeline's science.
AA Strategy & Ops Indexcapability0.125End-to-end office workflows in business apps: AutomationBench tool use 35%, AA-Briefcase agentic knowledge work 30%, AA-Omniscience business knowledge 25%, GDP.pdf and non-hallucination 5% each.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: strategy_and_ops_index (121 models)2026-11-22not applicable121 of 309The most tool-loop-heavy index on the Free route, and the one furthest from the Intelligence Index (r 0.91); its tool loops are business apps, not a terminal or a test suite.
Arena Agent bash reliabilitypreference0.029How often the agent's shell commands ran without failing, on Arena's live agentic tasks; failures outside its control (network, permissions, missing prerequisites) are not counted.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: bash reliability (61 models)2026-11-22not applicable61 of 309Each command is judged by an LLM, and Arena itself gives this signal half the weight of the others in its own net score.
Arena Agent net improvementpreference0.029How often an agent run left the user's repository better than it found it, net of the runs that made it worse.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: net improvement (61 models); Arena Agent leaderboard, tool-use tasks (style control on) (14 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on75 of 309Net of self-reported harm: a user who does not notice the damage does not report it.
Arena Agent praise net of complaintspreference0.029How often users praised the agent's work in the session, net of how often they complained about it.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: praise net of complaints (61 models)2026-11-22not applicable61 of 309Sentiment, not outcome: it tracks net improvement closely (r 0.97 on the 49 models both carry) and needs a user in the loop to exist at all.
Arena Agent steerabilitypreference0.029How often the agent changed course when the user redirected it part-way through a task.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: steerability (61 models); Arena Agent leaderboard, tool-use tasks (style control on) (14 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on75 of 309Judged by the user who redirected it, so it scores compliance as that user saw it, not whether the new course was the right one.
Arena Agent success ratepreference0.029Share of Arena's live agentic tasks the model finished, judged by the humans who set them.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: confirmed success (61 models); Arena Agent leaderboard, tool-use tasks (style control on) (14 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on75 of 309Task mix is whatever users brought that week, and a model routed to easier requests looks better than one that is not.
Arena Agent tool hallucination (negated)preference0.029How rarely the agent called a tool that does not exist or passed one arguments it does not take; negated, so higher is fewer.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: tool hallucination (negated: higher is fewer) (61 models); Arena Agent leaderboard, tool-use tasks (style control on) (14 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on75 of 309A malformed call the harness quietly repaired is not counted, so the rate is partly the scaffold's.
Arena Coding Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on coding prompts in the open text arena.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, coding category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, coding (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309Correlates hard with Arena's general text Elo, so read it as the coding-flavoured slice of one preference ranking, not as a second opinion about code.
Arena Creative Writing Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on creative-writing prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, creative writing category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, creative writing (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309The closest thing in the set to a prose-quality vote, and still a vote about taste rather than about whether the piece is true.
Arena Expert Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes from the subset of users Arena classes as domain experts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, expert category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on159 of 309Expertise is inferred from usage, not credentialed, and the subset is small enough to move on a slow week.
Arena Hard Prompts Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes restricted to the prompts Arena's own classifier calls hard.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, hard prompts category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, hard prompts (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309"Hard" is a classifier's judgement, and the classifier was trained on the same traffic the board scores.
Arena Instruction Following Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes where the prompt carried explicit constraints to obey.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, instruction following category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, instruction following (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309A voter checks the constraints they noticed; the ones they did not are not scored.
Arena Longer Query Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on the long tail of long prompts — the shape a drafting brief actually has.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, longer query category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, longer query (style control on) (1 model)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on160 of 309Published uncontrolled on some captures, so length habit can sit inside a board that is already about length.
Arena Math Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on mathematical prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, math category (style control on) (149 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on155 of 309Voters grade a worked answer they mostly cannot check, so presentation carries further here than elsewhere.
Arena Multi-turn Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on conversations that ran past one exchange, so the answer has to hold what was said before it.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, multi-turn category (style control on) (154 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on160 of 309The voter judges the turn they read last, so an early mistake the model carried forward quietly can go unscored.
Arena Text Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes over every prompt in the text arena, all categories pooled — the board the category slices are cut from.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, overall (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (8 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309One voting pool's taste, with length and markdown regressed out; every text category board here is a slice of the same votes.
Arena Text factuality Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on which answer got its facts right, over the text arena's prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text factuality leaderboard (125 models)2026-11-22not applicable125 of 309A voter judges the facts they can check, so a confident error on something they do not know reads as correct. It still orders the pool apart from the overall text vote (r 0.97, not a copy of it).
Arena WebDev Elopreference0.029Blind pairwise votes on rendered web artifacts — the only board here that scores something a person looked at rather than read.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena WebDev leaderboard, own Elo scale (115 models); Arena WebDev leaderboard, own Elo scale (no style toggle) (5 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22not applicable120 of 309Published uncontrolled, so visual polish and verbosity are inside the score rather than adjusted out of it.

Chat overall

Conversational use: what a person sees when they chat with the model.

wheel to zoom · drag to pan · double-click to reset · click a point to pin its card

114 models on the chart. Best value, cheapest first: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (default) → MiMo-V2.6-Flash (default) → GLM 5.3 Flash (default) → MiMo-V2.6-Pro (default), and 4 more.

How to read this chart

What this group is. Conversational use: what a person sees when they chat with the model. The preference half is the whole text arena, the slices of it a conversation runs through — hard prompts, several turns, stated constraints, prose, maths, expert questions, long queries — and the vote on whether the answer's facts were right; the capability half is the composite index and the Legal Capability Index, the least tool-loop-heavy of the six (30%) and the heaviest on what a chat answer needs: knowledge recall, non-hallucination, HLE-Diamond reasoning and long-document synthesis (70% together). Coding, WebDev, Search and the Agent arena are left out, and so are the other Capability Indexes: each is 35% or more tool loops or code (Strategy & Ops 65%), or repeats Legal (Finance, Economics, r 0.99).

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

71 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used — which boards bought this score

Weights are the flattened ones the ranker multiplies by, so the column sums to 1.000. Models covered counts the paid variants carrying a score on that board, out of every paid variant ranked. Style control is Arena's adjustment for length and formatting habit, and it is a property of the capture, not of the board.

Across those flattened weights the pillars carry capability 50%, preference 50% — equal halves by construction, with each pillar's boards sharing its half equally unless the group says otherwise.

boardpillarweightwhat it measuressourcecapturedstyle controlmodels coveredwhat would make it wrong
AA Intelligence Index v5capability0.250Artificial Analysis' composite of its re-run reasoning, knowledge and coding evaluations, per reasoning effort: version 5.0, which replaced v4.3 by 28 Oct 2026 and is scored only on the models AA has re-run on it.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: intelligence_index_v5 (112 models)2026-11-22not applicable112 of 309A composite, so it moves when its components saturate. Terminal- Bench 4.0 is one of its nine components, so a group weighting both reads that run twice; the Engineering Index tracks it at r 0.994, which is why no group weights the two together.
AA Legal Indexcapability0.250Legal recall and long-document work: AA-Omniscience legal knowledge 30%, AA-Briefcase 25%, HLE-Diamond 15%, non-hallucination 15%, GDP.pdf long-context documents 10%, AutomationBench 5%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: legal_index (119 models)2026-11-22not applicable119 of 309The least agentic index (30% tool loops) and the heaviest on factuality and long documents, but the knowledge it recalls is law, not this pipeline's science.
Arena Creative Writing Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes on creative-writing prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, creative writing category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, creative writing (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309The closest thing in the set to a prose-quality vote, and still a vote about taste rather than about whether the piece is true.
Arena Expert Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes from the subset of users Arena classes as domain experts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, expert category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on159 of 309Expertise is inferred from usage, not credentialed, and the subset is small enough to move on a slow week.
Arena Hard Prompts Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes restricted to the prompts Arena's own classifier calls hard.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, hard prompts category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, hard prompts (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309"Hard" is a classifier's judgement, and the classifier was trained on the same traffic the board scores.
Arena Instruction Following Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes where the prompt carried explicit constraints to obey.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, instruction following category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, instruction following (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309A voter checks the constraints they noticed; the ones they did not are not scored.
Arena Longer Query Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes on the long tail of long prompts — the shape a drafting brief actually has.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, longer query category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, longer query (style control on) (1 model)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on160 of 309Published uncontrolled on some captures, so length habit can sit inside a board that is already about length.
Arena Math Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes on mathematical prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, math category (style control on) (149 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on155 of 309Voters grade a worked answer they mostly cannot check, so presentation carries further here than elsewhere.
Arena Multi-turn Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes on conversations that ran past one exchange, so the answer has to hold what was said before it.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, multi-turn category (style control on) (154 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on160 of 309The voter judges the turn they read last, so an early mistake the model carried forward quietly can go unscored.
Arena Text Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes over every prompt in the text arena, all categories pooled — the board the category slices are cut from.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, overall (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (8 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309One voting pool's taste, with length and markdown regressed out; every text category board here is a slice of the same votes.
Arena Text factuality Elopreference0.056Blind pairwise votes on which answer got its facts right, over the text arena's prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text factuality leaderboard (125 models)2026-11-22not applicable125 of 309A voter judges the facts they can check, so a confident error on something they do not know reads as correct. It still orders the pool apart from the overall text vote (r 0.97, not a copy of it).

Task average

How well each model does across the four task groups that follow, averaged.

wheel to zoom · drag to pan · double-click to reset · click a point to pin its card

115 models on the chart. Best value, cheapest first: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (default) → MiMo-V2.6-Flash (default) → GPT-6 Luna (max) → GLM 5.3 Flash (default), and 6 more.

How to read this chart

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

72 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used

This tab has no boards of its own: its raw capability is the mean of the four task groups', so its evidence is theirs. The benchmarks-used table of each task group applies unchanged; overall and chat-overall are not in it.

Only a model scored in all four task groups, with an Arena rating in each and a solid dot on each group's own tab, can be best value here. A model missing a group, scored on capability boards alone in any, or greyed as thinly measured in any, shows the mean of the groups it has as a greyed, thinly measured dot, and is kept off the line and the presets.

Coding experiments

Writing and running experiment code in a sandbox is tool use first: the model that drives a terminal reliably beats the model that writes a prettier patch it never gets to apply.

wheel to zoom · drag to pan · double-click to reset · click a point to pin its card

115 models on the chart. Best value, cheapest first: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (default) → Muse Ember (max) → DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) → Hy4 (default), and 5 more.

How to read this chart

What this group is. Writing and running experiment code in a sandbox is tool use first: the model that drives a terminal reliably beats the model that writes a prettier patch it never gets to apply. So the preference half is Arena's agentic boards and the two coding votes, and the capability half is every re-run board that puts a model in front of a terminal, a test suite or a tool loop. On the v2 Free route our key reads that is two composites: the Engineering Capability Index, the only one with a terminal or a code run inside it (Terminal-Bench 4.0 and FrontierCode 2.0 15%, CritPt and Terminal-Bench-Science 20%), and the Strategy & Ops index, the most tool-loop-heavy (AutomationBench 35%, AA-Briefcase 30%); the two correlate at r 0.895, well clear of a duplicate. The Intelligence Index stays out as before: Engineering repeats it (r 0.994). The brief for one of these steps is scored here too: `gen_plan.*` writes the instructions a later step runs against, it reads the same repository and the same tools the step will, and the evidence that answers for the step is the evidence that answers for its plan.

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

59 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used — which boards bought this score

Weights are the flattened ones the ranker multiplies by, so the column sums to 1.000. Models covered counts the paid variants carrying a score on that board, out of every paid variant ranked. Style control is Arena's adjustment for length and formatting habit, and it is a property of the capture, not of the board.

Across those flattened weights the pillars carry capability 50%, preference 50% — equal halves by construction, with each pillar's boards sharing its half equally unless the group says otherwise.

boardpillarweightwhat it measuressourcecapturedstyle controlmodels coveredwhat would make it wrong
AA Engineering Indexcapability0.250Engineering recall, research science and agentic coding: AA-Omniscience engineering knowledge 30%, CritPt v2 Hard and Terminal-Bench-Science 20%, HLE-Diamond 20%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and FrontierCode 2.0 15%, AA-Briefcase 15%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: engineering_index (112 models)2026-11-22not applicable112 of 309The only Free board with a terminal or a code run in it, and only a third of it is; it orders the pool like the Intelligence Index (r 0.994), so the two never share a group.
AA Strategy & Ops Indexcapability0.250End-to-end office workflows in business apps: AutomationBench tool use 35%, AA-Briefcase agentic knowledge work 30%, AA-Omniscience business knowledge 25%, GDP.pdf and non-hallucination 5% each.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: strategy_and_ops_index (121 models)2026-11-22not applicable121 of 309The most tool-loop-heavy index on the Free route, and the one furthest from the Intelligence Index (r 0.91); its tool loops are business apps, not a terminal or a test suite.
Arena Agent net improvementpreference0.125How often an agent run left the user's repository better than it found it, net of the runs that made it worse.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: net improvement (61 models); Arena Agent leaderboard, tool-use tasks (style control on) (14 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on75 of 309Net of self-reported harm: a user who does not notice the damage does not report it.
Arena Agent success ratepreference0.125Share of Arena's live agentic tasks the model finished, judged by the humans who set them.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Agent leaderboard: confirmed success (61 models); Arena Agent leaderboard, tool-use tasks (style control on) (14 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on75 of 309Task mix is whatever users brought that week, and a model routed to easier requests looks better than one that is not.
Arena Coding Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on coding prompts in the open text arena.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, coding category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, coding (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309Correlates hard with Arena's general text Elo, so read it as the coding-flavoured slice of one preference ranking, not as a second opinion about code.
Arena WebDev Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on rendered web artifacts — the only board here that scores something a person looked at rather than read.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena WebDev leaderboard, own Elo scale (115 models); Arena WebDev leaderboard, own Elo scale (no style toggle) (5 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22not applicable120 of 309Published uncontrolled, so visual polish and verbosity are inside the score rather than adjusted out of it.

Research reasoning

Originating and checking a hypothesis is knowledge and reasoning with retrieval on top.

wheel to zoom · drag to pan · double-click to reset · click a point to pin its card

114 models on the chart. Best value, cheapest first: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (default) → GPT-6 Luna (max) → GLM 5.3 Flash (default) → MiMo-V2.6-Pro (default), and 3 more.

How to read this chart

What this group is. Originating and checking a hypothesis is knowledge and reasoning with retrieval on top, so the preference half is the hard, mathematical and expert Elos and the text factuality vote (a hypothesis built on a wrong fact is wrong), and the capability half is the composite index and the Economics Capability Index: of the six it carries the most HLE-Diamond (25%), the one expert reasoning exam left on the Free route, with quantitative modelling and long-report reading (GDP.pdf 10%), and it is not a duplicate of the Intelligence Index (r 0.972). Engineering would fit as well, research-level science and HLE-Diamond, and is left out because it repeats the Intelligence Index (r 0.994). Retrieval itself is read by no live board: Arena's search Elo and search factuality fit it and are stopped (below), and no re-run board in this file scores search over the live web on enough of the pool to order it. `gen_strat` and `gen_plan.research` sit here for the same reason the hypothesis steps do: choosing what a round will try, and briefing the research that will try it, is reasoning over what is known and what can be found out.

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

Which model each job gets

The pick for every job in the pipeline, at each quality preset and on each agent backend, read straight off this date’s ranking — with the reasoning effort to run it at. A dash is a backend that can route nothing.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

71 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used — which boards bought this score

Weights are the flattened ones the ranker multiplies by, so the column sums to 1.000. Models covered counts the paid variants carrying a score on that board, out of every paid variant ranked. Style control is Arena's adjustment for length and formatting habit, and it is a property of the capture, not of the board.

Across those flattened weights the pillars carry capability 50%, preference 50% — equal halves by construction, with each pillar's boards sharing its half equally unless the group says otherwise.

boardpillarweightwhat it measuressourcecapturedstyle controlmodels coveredwhat would make it wrong
AA Economics Indexcapability0.250Economics recall and quantitative work: AA-Briefcase 35%, AA-Omniscience economics knowledge 30%, HLE-Diamond 25%, GDP.pdf long economic reports 10%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: economics_index (119 models)2026-11-22not applicable119 of 309The heaviest on HLE-Diamond of the six, and a near-copy of the Legal and Finance indexes (r 0.99), so no group weights it beside either.
AA Intelligence Index v5capability0.250Artificial Analysis' composite of its re-run reasoning, knowledge and coding evaluations, per reasoning effort: version 5.0, which replaced v4.3 by 28 Oct 2026 and is scored only on the models AA has re-run on it.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: intelligence_index_v5 (112 models)2026-11-22not applicable112 of 309A composite, so it moves when its components saturate. Terminal- Bench 4.0 is one of its nine components, so a group weighting both reads that run twice; the Engineering Index tracks it at r 0.994, which is why no group weights the two together.
Arena Expert Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes from the subset of users Arena classes as domain experts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, expert category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on159 of 309Expertise is inferred from usage, not credentialed, and the subset is small enough to move on a slow week.
Arena Hard Prompts Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes restricted to the prompts Arena's own classifier calls hard.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, hard prompts category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, hard prompts (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309"Hard" is a classifier's judgement, and the classifier was trained on the same traffic the board scores.
Arena Math Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on mathematical prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, math category (style control on) (149 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on155 of 309Voters grade a worked answer they mostly cannot check, so presentation carries further here than elsewhere.
Arena Text factuality Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on which answer got its facts right, over the text arena's prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text factuality leaderboard (125 models)2026-11-22not applicable125 of 309A voter judges the facts they can check, so a confident error on something they do not know reads as correct. It still orders the pool apart from the overall text vote (r 0.97, not a copy of it).

Scientific writing

Drafting a paper is long-form generation held to a brief.

wheel to zoom · drag to pan · double-click to reset · click a point to pin its card

114 models on the chart. Best value, cheapest first: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (default) → MiMo-V2.6-Flash (default) → GPT-6 Luna (max) → GLM 5.3 Flash (default), and 4 more.

How to read this chart

What this group is. Drafting a paper is long-form generation held to a brief, so the preference half is the creative, long-query and instruction-following Elos — the places humans vote on written prose — and the text factuality vote, because a paper that states a wrong fact fails however it reads; the capability half is the composite index and the Legal Capability Index, the one of the six built most on producing and synthesising long documents with the facts right: argumentation, GDP.pdf document deliverables (10%, the most of any index), non-hallucination (15%) and HLE-Diamond (15%), with the least tool-loop share (30%).

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

71 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used — which boards bought this score

Weights are the flattened ones the ranker multiplies by, so the column sums to 1.000. Models covered counts the paid variants carrying a score on that board, out of every paid variant ranked. Style control is Arena's adjustment for length and formatting habit, and it is a property of the capture, not of the board.

Across those flattened weights the pillars carry capability 50%, preference 50% — equal halves by construction, with each pillar's boards sharing its half equally unless the group says otherwise.

boardpillarweightwhat it measuressourcecapturedstyle controlmodels coveredwhat would make it wrong
AA Intelligence Index v5capability0.250Artificial Analysis' composite of its re-run reasoning, knowledge and coding evaluations, per reasoning effort: version 5.0, which replaced v4.3 by 28 Oct 2026 and is scored only on the models AA has re-run on it.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: intelligence_index_v5 (112 models)2026-11-22not applicable112 of 309A composite, so it moves when its components saturate. Terminal- Bench 4.0 is one of its nine components, so a group weighting both reads that run twice; the Engineering Index tracks it at r 0.994, which is why no group weights the two together.
AA Legal Indexcapability0.250Legal recall and long-document work: AA-Omniscience legal knowledge 30%, AA-Briefcase 25%, HLE-Diamond 15%, non-hallucination 15%, GDP.pdf long-context documents 10%, AutomationBench 5%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: legal_index (119 models)2026-11-22not applicable119 of 309The least agentic index (30% tool loops) and the heaviest on factuality and long documents, but the knowledge it recalls is law, not this pipeline's science.
Arena Creative Writing Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on creative-writing prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, creative writing category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, creative writing (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309The closest thing in the set to a prose-quality vote, and still a vote about taste rather than about whether the piece is true.
Arena Instruction Following Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes where the prompt carried explicit constraints to obey.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, instruction following category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, instruction following (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309A voter checks the constraints they noticed; the ones they did not are not scored.
Arena Longer Query Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on the long tail of long prompts — the shape a drafting brief actually has.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, longer query category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, longer query (style control on) (1 model)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on160 of 309Published uncontrolled on some captures, so length habit can sit inside a board that is already about length.
Arena Text factuality Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on which answer got its facts right, over the text arena's prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text factuality leaderboard (125 models)2026-11-22not applicable125 of 309A voter judges the facts they can check, so a confident error on something they do not know reads as correct. It still orders the pool apart from the overall text vote (r 0.97, not a copy of it).

Review judging

Reviewing a submission is reading something long against a brief and saying where it fails.

wheel to zoom · drag to pan · double-click to reset · click a point to pin its card

97 models on the chart. Best value, cheapest first: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (default) → GPT-6 Luna (max) → GLM 5.3 Flash (default) → MiMo-V2.6-Pro (default), and 3 more.

How to read this chart

What this group is. Reviewing a submission is reading something long against a brief and saying where it fails, so the preference half is the hard, instruction-following and expert Elos and the text factuality vote (a reviewer has to notice a wrong fact), and the capability half is the composite index and the Healthcare & Medical Capability Index: the only index carrying MLCR, AA's long-context reasoning run (15%), with non-hallucination (10%) and HLE-Diamond (10%), and its task is synthesising long records against what they should say.

Across: effective cost on a log scale — the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, with the reference model at 1x. Up: raw capability, 0-100, fitted over the boards each variant was itself measured on and nothing else.

A filled dot joined by the dashed line is on the Pareto frontier: nothing plotted beats it on cost and capability at once. A hollow dashed dot is measured too thinly to hold that line; that includes every model scored on capability boards alone, with no Arena rating, which is never on the line or in a preset. The grey ring around a dot is the share of this group’s benchmark weight the row was not measured on, and a green ring marks a model released in the 30 days before the selected date.

Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Hover a point for its card and click it to pin the card; type in the box to dim every name that does not match, and untick a marker kind to drop it. Hovering a table row below lights up its point.

Which model each job gets

The pick for every job in the pipeline, at each quality preset and on each agent backend, read straight off this date’s ranking — with the reasoning effort to run it at. A dash is a backend that can route nothing.

How to read this table

Click any column header to sort by it; the rows arrive frontier first, then by raw capability — the axis the frontier itself is drawn on, so no row here sits above one that beats it on both cost and capability at once. Click a row to open that model in the per-model drilldown at the foot of the page.

Capability per cost is a mean of min-max-scaled thirds, one of which (cost per task) a price-only row does not have, so it is a column to read rather than an order to rank by. Human votes and benchmark tests are the two halves capability is the mean of — the same fit recomputed over the blind-preference boards and over the scored benchmark boards on their own, the preference and capability pillars elsewhere on this page. They read - where a model carries less than half of one pillar’s weight, and a wide gap between the two is a finding about the model, not a defect in the table.

Boards and evidence say how much of the group the row was actually run on — how many of its benchmarks, and what share of their weight — and uncertainty is the standard error the fit puts on the ability. Capability is raw capability on the 0-100 scale and cost is effective cost as a multiple of the reference model; the method section defines both in full.

54 least-measured models in this group

The ranked rows with the least of this group's benchmark weight behind them. Every score here is the row's own boards, or the distance from another effort of the same model where the status says placed relative to, and few boards make a wide band: read the ability band beside each. The ones marked thinly measured were kept off the frontier for that reason — they are drawn as hollow dashed dots on the chart.

Benchmarks used — which boards bought this score

Weights are the flattened ones the ranker multiplies by, so the column sums to 1.000. Models covered counts the paid variants carrying a score on that board, out of every paid variant ranked. Style control is Arena's adjustment for length and formatting habit, and it is a property of the capture, not of the board.

Across those flattened weights the pillars carry capability 50%, preference 50% — equal halves by construction, with each pillar's boards sharing its half equally unless the group says otherwise.

boardpillarweightwhat it measuressourcecapturedstyle controlmodels coveredwhat would make it wrong
AA Healthcare & Medical Indexcapability0.250Clinical knowledge and record synthesis: AA-Omniscience medical knowledge 25%, AA-Briefcase 25%, MLCR long-context reasoning 15%, AutomationBench 15%, non-hallucination 10%, HLE-Diamond 10%.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: healthcare_and_medical_index (99 models)2026-11-22not applicable99 of 309The only index carrying MLCR, AA's long-context reasoning run, and run on fewer models than the others (it needs every component).
AA Intelligence Index v5capability0.250Artificial Analysis' composite of its re-run reasoning, knowledge and coding evaluations, per reasoning effort: version 5.0, which replaced v4.3 by 28 Oct 2026 and is scored only on the models AA has re-run on it.Artificial Analysis API - Artificial Analysis API: intelligence_index_v5 (112 models)2026-11-22not applicable112 of 309A composite, so it moves when its components saturate. Terminal- Bench 4.0 is one of its nine components, so a group weighting both reads that run twice; the Engineering Index tracks it at r 0.994, which is why no group weights the two together.
Arena Expert Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes from the subset of users Arena classes as domain experts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, expert category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models)2026-09-16 to 2026-11-22on159 of 309Expertise is inferred from usage, not credentialed, and the subset is small enough to move on a slow week.
Arena Hard Prompts Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes restricted to the prompts Arena's own classifier calls hard.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, hard prompts category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, hard prompts (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309"Hard" is a classifier's judgement, and the classifier was trained on the same traffic the board scores.
Arena Instruction Following Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes where the prompt carried explicit constraints to obey.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text leaderboard, instruction following category (style control on) (153 models); Arena text leaderboard, all categories (style control on) (6 models); Arena text leaderboard, instruction following (style control on) (2 models)2026-09-13 to 2026-11-22on161 of 309A voter checks the constraints they noticed; the ones they did not are not scored.
Arena Text factuality Elopreference0.125Blind pairwise votes on which answer got its facts right, over the text arena's prompts.Arena leaderboards (lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset, CC-BY-4.0) - Arena Text factuality leaderboard (125 models)2026-11-22not applicable125 of 309A voter judges the facts they can check, so a confident error on something they do not know reads as correct. It still orders the pool apart from the overall text vote (r 0.97, not a copy of it).
