Capability per cost is the ranking key, and it is the mean of three equal thirds, each min-max scaled over the models present: list-price cheapness (0.3334), cost-per-task cheapness (0.3333) and raw capability (0.3333). A model has to earn its place on all three; no single axis can carry it. The name is a name, not a sum you can do: the three thirds are averaged, never divided one by another. The two cost thirds are scaled in log space, because price spans three orders of magnitude here and a linear scale would flatten everything under a dollar into one clump.

Nothing here is filled in. A variant is scored on the boards it was itself measured on at its own reasoning effort, and on no others: no board is carried over from another effort, another model or a ratio, and a variant no same-source cost ratio reaches has no cost per task at all rather than a guessed one. Its capability per cost is then the two thirds it has, renormalised, and its row says price-only, no cost-per-task data.

The scores come from one fit per group, over exactly the cells that exist. Every board is put on a 0-100 scale by its own median and inter-quartile range, so a board the pool is near-flat on uses about a third of the scale rather than being stretched across all of it. Then one least-squares fit reads every score in the group at once as two numbers added together: a level for the board and an ability for the variant, each cell weighted by its board's weight. The board level absorbs how hard or how generous a board is; the ability that is left is the raw capability printed here. Two variants that share boards are compared through those boards; two that do not are compared through the chain of variants connecting them. That is why a model measured on the easy half of a group no longer outranks one measured on the hard half, and why nothing had to be invented to get there.

Efforts of one model are placed against each other. The fit has a level per board and an ability per row and no term for the two together, so a weakness the whole model shares on boards only one of its efforts was run on lands on that effort alone. So the best-measured effort of a model keeps the fit's ability, and each other effort is placed at that ability plus the weighted mean gap between the two on the boards both were measured on — above it where it beats it there. Under 1 shared boards the row keeps the fit's own answer and says so.

Unmeasured rows are named, not scored. A variant measured on fewer than 2 of a group's boards, or on one pillar's boards only, is left out of that group's fit, chart and table, and named in the not-scored fold under the group instead. What a scored row carries is two columns: measured boards, how many of the group's boards it sits on, and evidence coverage, the share of the group's benchmark weight those boards are, out of the boards it could have been run on: a board its source had stopped running before the row was released does not count against it. The ability band is the standard error the fit itself puts on that row, so a row on two boards carries a visibly wider band than one on fifteen, and the ring around a dot is the weight the row was not measured on.

Read a sparse row as optimistic. Which boards a lab publishes is not a coin toss: a model is entered where it does well, so across this catalogue a row's coverage and its score rise together. The fit cannot correct for that — the missing cells are missing — so it is left visible instead: a row on two boards with a wide band and a heavy ring is the page saying the number is the best of what was published, not the average of what was run.

A thin row is scored, but it may not define a frontier. The frontier is the one thing on this page a reader takes at face value, and a row on a quarter of a group's weight should not hold its cheap end however well that quarter went. So a row also has to carry enough of the group's weight to be on it. One that does not says thinly measured in its status, is drawn as a hollow dashed dot, and is listed in the least-measured fold under its group. and on enough boards of its own — two bars, both read off what was run at this row's own reasoning effort. A row placed against another effort of the same model inherits neither: its number leans on its anchor, which is exactly why it may not draw the line in its anchor's place, so an anchor can sit on a frontier its own placed siblings are held off. The status of a barred row names the bar it fell under. Where the two bars sit is two numbers, shrinkage: in .claude/skills/amg-llm-bench/data/task_groups.yaml.

What the tabs are. Overall and Chat overall read the boards with no pipeline step behind them, so no tool-calling floor and no preset cut. The 4 task groups score the work the pipeline's steps do, and Task average is their mean — nothing else is averaged into it. Nothing but evidence keeps a model out of a group. A model is ranked in a group once that group's boards have measured it on at least one Arena board and one Artificial Analysis board, and not before; no judgement about what the model is for enters.

The two pillars — preference, blind human pairwise votes on Arena, and capability, Artificial Analysis' re-run fixed task sets — are fitted separately and averaged, so each carries half of every group however many boards it holds — the alternative, one flat fit over every cell, quietly hands the ranking to whichever pillar published the most numbers. A pillar column is filled in wherever the row has one measured board of it; where it has none the column reads -, the row says pillar missing, and the raw capability beside it is the pillar that remains. A row measured in fewer than two pillars is not ranked at all: one kind of evidence is a reading, not a verdict.

Every column on this page, in plain words:

capability per cost
how good the model is, set against what it costs: the mean of three equal thirds, each min-max scaled over the plotted variants.
raw capability (0-100)
how well the model suits this group's work, from the group's own benchmark weights.
human votes (preference)
the same fit run over this group's Arena boards alone — blind human votes; `-` where the row carries no Arena board here at all. The raw capability is the mean of the pillar columns.
benchmark tests (capability)
the same fit over the group's Artificial Analysis boards alone. A wide gap between the two pillar columns is a finding about the model, not an error.
effective cost (x reference)
the geometric mean of relative list price and relative cost per task, as a multiple of the reference model.
evidence coverage
the share of the group's benchmark weight this variant was measured on, at its own reasoning effort. Nothing else is behind the row: an unmeasured board is left out, not filled in.
measured boards
how many of the group's boards this variant has a measured row on, out of how many the group weighs.
ability band
the standard error of this row's ability in the least-squares fit: how far the raw capability could move on the evidence behind it. It narrows with boards measured, never with boards borrowed.

Every status a row can carry:

best value
nothing is both cheaper and a better fit.
beaten on value
something else is cheaper and fits better at once.
thinly measured
this row was not itself measured on enough of the group to be allowed on the frontier, and the status says which bar it fell under: the boards of its own it was run on, the share of the group's weight behind it, or both. Nothing is inherited — an effort placed against a better-measured sibling is judged on what was run at its own effort. It is still scored, ranked, plotted and listed among the least-measured models; a row nobody has really measured simply cannot set the line the rest of the page is read against.
price-only, no cost-per-task data
no same-source ratio reaches this model, so it has no cost per task at all. Nothing is invented for it: its capability per cost is the list-price and raw-capability thirds alone, and its effective cost on the chart is its list price.
no cost-per-task data at this reasoning effort
the model is priced per task but nobody published a cost multiplier for this effort, and the default effort's cost is not this effort's cost. The row is treated as having none.
pillar missing
nobody measured this row on any board of that pillar, so the column is blank and the raw capability is the pillar that remains — which means a different thing from a mean over both, and says so. A row missing a pillar is not ranked at all unless another effort of the same model carries it.
effort cost measured
a published run priced this model at this reasoning effort against another effort of itself, so the cost on this row is the effort's own cost.
placed relative to
this row is an effort variant of a model whose best-measured variant sits on more boards, so each of its pillars is that variant's pillar plus the weighted mean gap between the two on the boards of that pillar both were measured on. A pillar they share no board in keeps this row's own reading where it has one, and the anchor's value only where it has none: a lead on Arena is a statement about preference and about nothing else. A global fit has no model-by-board term, so a family-wide weakness on the boards only one variant was run on would otherwise be charged to that variant alone.
no board shared with
this effort variant and its family's best-measured variant were never run on the same board, so there is no distance between the two to read. It keeps whatever the group's own fit gave it, and gets no number at all if the fit never reached it.
free listing exists
the same model also has a free listing on the same id, with a :free suffix. That lane is throttled and temporary, so the ranking still prices the model at its paid list price.

Where this is weakest, in the data's own words:

  • overall: Humanity's Last Exam, AA-LCR, SciCode and Terminal-Bench 4.0 were read here until 29 Oct 2026 and left because the v2 Free route our key reads does not serve them; they return with a Pro key. The capability half is now composites of a few shared runs, one evaluation family. Equal shares are breadth, not judgement: a board sold as one narrow thing counts as much as the whole text arena, and the Agent arena's six measures carry six shares on under a fifth of the pool. No re-run maths board is left: AIME, AIME 2025 and MATH-500 stopped getting new models (and the math index left the API on 2026-10-29), so maths is read through Arena's Math vote alone. GPQA, IFBench, MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Hard, tau2, tau-Banking and the Document arena were read here until 29 Oct 2026 and left because their sources no longer score new releases on them. The Search arena and its factuality vote left on 9 Nov 2026 for the same reason (nothing released after 29 Sep 2026 on either); they come back by the §4 test when Arena rates this month's models on them.
  • chat-overall: Humanity's Last Exam and AA-LCR were the knowledge exam and long-context board here until 29 Oct 2026; the v2 Free route our key reads does not serve them, and they return with a Pro key. Legal stands in as a borderline fit: its knowledge is law, and a quarter of it is AA-Briefcase agentic work. It says nothing about tool use: a model that chats well and cannot call a tool ranks here on its chat alone. No re-run maths or instruction-following board is left in the capability half (AIME, MMLU-Pro, GPQA and IFBench stopped getting new models and left on 29 Oct 2026, with the Document arena), so maths is Arena's Math vote and stated constraints are Arena's Instruction Following vote.
  • coding-experiments: Arena's two agentic boards are the only human read of agent behaviour anywhere in this file, and they cover a fraction of the pool; until that widens the preference half here leans on the WebDev and coding Elos, which are votes about text. Nothing in the capability half scores a patch against a real repository's own test suite any more — SWE-bench went with the hand-transcribed boards — so what is left reads terminal and tool behaviour instead. A reproducible SWE-bench capture is the single biggest thing this group is missing. AutomationBench is served on its own only by the v2 Pro route (`automationbench_aa`, which the capture would record as a new board for review); on the Free route it reaches this group inside Strategy & Ops. Terminal- Bench 4.0 was not either when it was dropped on 2026-09-18; the API has served it as `terminalbench_v4_0` since, and it is read here again from 2026-10-28. Terminal-Bench 2.1 and LiveCodeBench left on 29 Oct 2026: Artificial Analysis no longer runs either on new releases. Terminal-Bench 4.0 and SciCode left the same day because the v2 Free route our key reads does not serve them (they return with a Pro key), which left this half with no board of its own; the fallback is the two Capability Indexes that carry terminal, code and tool-loop runs. Both are borderline fits — most of Engineering is engineering-discipline recall and science reasoning, and Strategy & Ops' tool loops are business apps — and they stand here because a half with one board stops the run (`max_board_weight`) and a half with none ranks nobody.
  • research-reasoning: Humanity's Last Exam and AA-LCR were the reasoning exam and the long-context board here until 29 Oct 2026; the v2 Free route our key reads does not serve them, and they return with a Pro key. Economics is a borderline stand-in: its knowledge is economics, not this pipeline's science, and 35% of it is AA-Briefcase agentic work. Nothing here reads retrieval as a re-run task: the search boards that exist run on a handful of models each, which is an anecdote wearing a board's clothes, so search was read through Arena's two search votes alone, and since 9 Nov 2026 not at all: both left that day because Arena has rated nothing released after 29 Sep 2026 on them (stopped_boards), and they return by the §4 test once it rates this month's models. GPQA left on 29 Oct 2026: Artificial Analysis no longer scores new releases on it, and AA-LCR came in for it. The Omniscience Index and CritPt were weighted here until 28 Oct 2026 and are not now: neither is in the Artificial Analysis API, so both were hand-copied once (2026-09-16) and only aged, CritPt reads one discipline, and the factuality votes now read what Omniscience stood in for on a live board. Nothing here measures whether a hypothesis was any good, which is the thing the step is for; the boards measure whether the model knows things and can find things.
  • scientific-writing: No benchmark measuring scientific or academic paper writing covers this pool, so the capability half is the composite index and the Legal index standing in for prose quality. AA-LCR was the long-context board here until 29 Oct 2026; the v2 Free route our key reads does not serve it, and it returns with a Pro key. No board grades the produced document any more: GDPval-PDF was a hand copy of 2026-09-16 the API never served, and it left with IFBench (no new releases scored) and the Document arena (not republished since 2026-09-13) on 29 Oct 2026; GDP.pdf comes back if the API ever serves it. The factuality vote checks facts as a voter knows them, not claims against a cited source; nothing in the group measures citation faithfulness or revision to reviewer comments. Read it as general writing preference held to a brief until such a board exists. `aa_aabriefcasetimepertask` was considered for this half and left out: it is a duration, not a quality, and a model that is fast at a briefcase task is not thereby better at writing a paper.
  • review-judging: AA-LCR was the long-context board here until 29 Oct 2026; the v2 Free route our key reads does not serve it, and it returns with a Pro key. Healthcare stands in as a borderline fit: its knowledge is clinical, and 40% of it is agentic work. Judging is the step with the least direct evidence anywhere in this file: no board here scores a review against what a conference's own reviewers said. The text factuality vote is the closest thing to "would it notice the claim is wrong"; the Omniscience Index read that until 28 Oct 2026, and was dropped as a hand-copied 2026-09-16 board nothing re-pulls, and GDPval-PDF and the Document arena left for the same reason on 29 Oct 2026 (a hand copy, and a board not republished since 2026-09-13). Until a review board exists this group is a proxy stack, and the `pillar missing` marks on thin rows are the honest part of it.
  • On no preference board at all, so that pillar is unmeasured for them rather than zero and what they are scored on is the pillar that remains: 122 rows.
  • On no capability board at all, so that pillar is unmeasured for them rather than zero and what they are scored on is the pillar that remains: 188 rows.
  • Effort multipliers were published for these models only, so effort is priced for them and unpriced everywhere else: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra.
  • Two runs that priced the same pair land a median of 2.53x apart (worst 5.84x, across 12 models). Treat that as the noise floor: a cost difference smaller than it means nothing.

Every claim above is recomputed from data/*.yaml on each run. The evidence blocks under each group, and the drilldown at the foot of the page, carry the raw numbers and the dated pages they came from.

Cost per task evidence

A ratio row may only relate two models measured on the same tasks in the same published run, so nothing here crosses sources. The chaining happens in the ranker, which solves the whole graph at once in log space with deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash pinned at 1.00 — which is why a fitted number matches no single source exactly.

Across the 12 models two or more runs both priced, the same pair comes out a median of 2.53x apart and at worst 5.84x apart. That is the noise floor under this whole axis: a cost gap smaller than it is not evidence of anything.

Effort multipliers

Effort is a cost dial, not a value one: one harness has Opus 5 solving fewer tasks at xhigh than at high while costing more. These price the dial and never move a raw-capability score. They exist for these models only. Every other model split by effort has no cost per task at any effort but its default: the default's cost is not that effort's cost and is not borrowed for it. Those rows say no cost-per-task data at this reasoning effort in their status and are placed on their list price alone.

Price evidence

List prices in $/M tokens, discounts deliberately ignored: a launch promotion or one cheap endpoint lapses, and the ladder should not reshuffle when it does. The blended proxy in this table averages the input price and the output price with output counted 3 times as heavily. That weighting is assumed: it is the pool-wide fallback that overall, chat overall and the task average are priced on, because no pipeline step measures them, while each task group is priced on its own steps' measured ratio. It is one number, price_blend: in .claude/skills/amg-llm-bench/data/task_groups.yaml, to change. A cheaper route, where one exists, is recorded and not scored.
